body.statement:
On \(\mathcal M^{\beta}_{K,\varepsilon}(B_{\mathrm H})\) with \(\beta>(d_X+1)/2\), can the handle \(\mathfrak F\), using tensor-product B-splines of total dimension \(s_n\asymp n^{(d_X+1)/(2\beta+d_X+1)}\), be completed by explicit spline boundary conventions, a constrained product-likelihood parameterization, and a local likelihood-curvature and empirical-process argument that prove all of the following for one raw fit?  First,
\[
 r_\pi+r_A+r_Z+r_f=O_P(\rho_n),
 \qquad \rho_n=n^{-\beta/(2\beta+d_X+1)}.
\]
Second, with \(\zeta_n=\rho_n\sqrt{\log n}\),
\[
 \|\widehat\pi-\pi\|_\infty+
 \|\widehat M_A-M_A\|_\infty+
 \|\widehat M_Z-M_Z\|_\infty+
 \|\widehat f-f\|_\infty=O_P(\zeta_n).
\]
Third, the empirical minimum modal-gap rule over the \(K!\) common permutations selects the population labeling with probability tending to one.  Fourth, after threshold-and-renormalize cleaning at a training-fold threshold satisfying \(\zeta_n=o(\tau_{S,n})\) and \(\tau_{S,n}=o(n^{-1/4})\), the fitted propensity, cleaned measurement matrices, cell probabilities, and posterior Gram matrix satisfy the declared computable half-margin restrictions.  The cleaned support-rate-window lemma proves that such a threshold is compatible with the stated smoothness and yields exact true-zero recovery.  What remains open is the likelihood-curvature, spline approximation, localization, and uniform-rate proof for this specifically prescribed global product-likelihood fit; no conclusion about \(R_\Sigma\) or \(\Delta_n\) is asserted merely from a list of coordinatewise \(L^2\) rates.
body.justification: The residual question is now falsifiable at the missing likelihood-curvature, spline, primitive L2, uniform-rate, label, and half-margin steps.
body.gap: The frozen smoothness assumptions and adjacent literature do not prove those facts for the specified global product likelihood.
body.consumer: Resolving it would turn the conditional efficient-inference theorem into a complete implementation guarantee on the smooth subclass.

obligation.what_is_open: A proof that the prescribed global tensor-product B-spline product likelihood satisfies the required local curvature and localization inequalities, attains the primitive L2 and uniform rates, selects the modal labeling, and enters the cleaned half-margin stratum.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen H"older assumptions do not specify a spline boundary or extension convention on the general outcome support, a constrained likelihood chart, a local likelihood-curvature inequality, or an empirical-process localization result.  The finite projector and support-cleaning algebra cannot supply those statistical facts.
obligation.attempted: The support-cleaning map, exact zero recovery, cleaned error bound, and an explicit threshold window were proved.  The remaining derived-operator propagation was reduced to finite inverse and conditional Gram perturbations once a primitive fit lies in the regular stratum.
obligation.partial_result: The threshold-and-renormalize algebra is closed.  Uniform raw measurement error \(r_{A,\infty}+r_{Z,\infty}=O_P(\rho_n\sqrt{\log n})\), together with \(\beta>(d_X+1)/2\), admits the explicit deterministic window \(\tau_{S,n}=\{\rho_n\sqrt{\log n}\,n^{-1/4}\}^{1/2}\); then \(\kappa_{\mathrm{supp},n}=o_P(1)\), \(\tau_{S,n}=o(n^{-1/4})\), true-zero cells are removed exactly, and \(r_A^c+r_Z^c=O_P(\rho_n+\tau_{S,n})=o_P(n^{-1/4})\), without beta-min.  Conditional on a label-aligned primitive fit attaining the displayed \(L^2\) and uniform rates and entering the computable half-margin stratum, bounded integration and the finite inverse, Bayes, projector, and fixed-rank pseudoinverse perturbation identities propagate the primitive errors through the cleaned-law plug-ins; the resulting products satisfy the inference window.  What remains unproved is that the specifically named global B-spline product-likelihood estimator attains those primitive rates and enters that stratum under only the frozen H\"older assumptions.
